messages.author: c945c8b58202c7e0
messages.subject: scan additional interacting QTL
parts:
Hi Karl,
I am running the scanone function for my mapping population (F4, 180 offsprings, 2000 markers), and I get one major QTL on chr6 and a minor one on chr14.
Since I see some background noise,  I want to fix the locus (marker) on chr6 and scan any additional interacting QTL across all the other chromosomes.
I am not sure if there is a function to do this in r/qtl, could you please help me out?
Thanks!


Best,
Qingming

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scan additional interacting QTL
parts:
There are two approaches for this:

First, you can pull out the genotypes for a marker near the QTL, and use that as an additive covariate in scanone(). With f4 data, you'd need to turn the marker genotypes into a two-column matrix of genotypes. To scan for interactive QTL, use the marker genotypes as an interactive covariate.

Alternatively, you can use makeqtl() and addqtl(). To scan for interactive QTL, you'll need to use a formula like y ~ Q1*Q2.

See http://rqtl.org/tutorials/rqtltour.pdf: steps 4-6 in Example 5 Multiple QTL mapping, pg 14
And the R/qtl book (http://rqtl.org/book), pages 206-208.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] omit AB genotype from plot.pxg
parts:
It seems like you maybe want to change the cross type to something else.
Like, maybe the data are being interpreted as an intercross but they are really RIL?

In read.cross, you can specify the cross type with the argument crosstype, for example crosstype="riself"
Alternatively, you could use a function like convert2riself() or convert2risib().

karl

the convert2riself() worked!
thank you, Karl

On Tue, Jun 27, 2017 at 4:04 PM, Gao, Qing-ming <qingmi...@uky.edu> wrote:
Thanks for your reply, Karl.
It's an intercross population; I wanna drop off the AB genotype in the plot just for better comparison cause the AB gives too much noise and not much informative. I will try the convert2riself() or convert2risib(). 


Best,
Qingming

On Tue, Jun 27, 2017 at 3:33 PM, Karl Broman <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
It seems like you maybe want to change the cross type to something else.
Like, maybe the data are being interpreted as an intercross but they are really RIL?

In read.cross, you can specify the cross type with the argument crosstype, for example crosstype="riself"
Alternatively, you could use a function like convert2riself() or convert2risib().

karl

> On Jun 27, 2017, at 3:02 PM, Gao, Qing-ming <qingmi...@uky.edu> wrote:
>
> Hi Karl,
> Thanks for your help!
> I just finished the QTL analysis and am writing the manuscript now.
> I have a question about the plot.pxg function, can I make a phenotype vs genotype plot only showing AA/BB but not other combinations?
> please see the attached plot, I want remove the AB genotype in the plot. Thank you!
>
> <Rplot.png>
>
> On Tue, May 30, 2017 at 9:48 AM, Karl Broman <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> My approach is to use a permutation test with a two-dimensional, two-QTL genome scan, and focus on penalized LOD scores as in Manichaikul et al (2009)
> https://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/multiqtl.pdf
>
> karl
>
>
> > On May 30, 2017, at 9:45 AM, Gao, Qing-ming <qingmi...@uky.edu> wrote:
> >
> > Hi Karl,
> > I tried the makeqtl() and addqtl() to scan the interactive QTL (y~Q1*Q2), and a possible interactive Q2 was picked with a lod value. But I am not sure how to decide if this lod value is significant. Do you have any idea?
> > Thanks!
> >
> > Qingming
> >
> > On Wed, May 24, 2017 at 5:56 PM, Karl Broman <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > There are two approaches for this:
> >
> > First, you can pull out the genotypes for a marker near the QTL, and use that as an additive covariate in scanone(). With f4 data, you'd need to turn the marker genotypes into a two-column matrix of genotypes. To scan for interactive QTL, use the marker genotypes as an interactive covariate.
> >
> > Alternatively, you can use makeqtl() and addqtl(). To scan for interactive QTL, you'll need to use a formula like y ~ Q1*Q2.
> >
> > See http://rqtl.org/tutorials/rqtltour.pdf: steps 4-6 in Example 5 Multiple QTL mapping, pg 14
> > And the R/qtl book (http://rqtl.org/book), pages 206-208.
> >
> > karl
> >
> > > On May 24, 2017, at 11:05 AM, Qing-ming Gao <qg...@g.uky.edu> wrote:
> > >
> > > Hi Karl,
> > > I am running the scanone function for my mapping population (F4, 180 offsprings, 2000 markers), and I get one major QTL on chr6 and a minor one on chr14.
> > > Since I see some background noise,  I want to fix the locus (marker) on chr6 and scan any additional interacting QTL across all the other chromosomes.
> > > I am not sure if there is a function to do this in r/qtl, could you please help me out?
> > > Thanks!
> > >
> > >
> > > Best,
> > > Qingming
